title: Subtraction with Numbers up to 20
seo_title: Grade 1 Subtraction within 20 Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 1)
standard_text: Illustrate subtraction involving numbers up to 20 using a variety of concrete and pictorial models; solve subtraction problems (given orally or in pictures) where both numbers are less than 20.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 subtraction worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: take away with pictures, subtract within 20, number lines and stories. 100 questions with pictures and answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Subtract means take away: 12 − 5 means start with 12 and take away 5.
  • Count back from the bigger number: 12 → 11, 10, 9, 8, 7.
  • Think addition: 5 + ☐ = 12, so 12 − 5 = 7.
  • Subtraction also compares: how many more, how many fewer.

Examples

Example

15 − 6

15 − 5 = 10

10 − 1

Answer: 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the startStart counting back from the next number.
Wrong orderStart with the bigger number.
Adding instead“Left” and “fewer” mean subtract.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 1 ask about subtraction?
faq.a: Illustrate subtraction involving numbers up to 20 using models, and solve subtraction problems where both numbers are less than 20.

faq.q: What words tell us to subtract?
faq.a: Left, take away, fewer, how many more.
Every subtraction fact has a related addition fact.

items.q: There are 7. 3 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 3. Count the ones with no X. 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: There are 9. 4 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 4. Count the ones with no X. 9 − 4 = 5.

items.q: Which one matches the picture?
items.e: There are 11. 4 are crossed out. 7 are left. 11 − 4 = 7.

items.q: Patricia sees 12 − 5. She says 17. What is right?
items.e: 17 is 12 + 5. Patricia added. Take away 5 from 12. 12 − 5 = 7.

items.q: There were 12. Now 8 are left. How many were taken away?
items.e: Count the ones with an X. 12 − 4 = 8. So 4 were taken away.

items.q: Jomar counts back for 12 − 3. He says “12, 11, 10.” What is right?
items.e: Do not say 12 again. Start after 12: 11, 10, 9. So 12 − 3 = 9.

items.q: What is 15 − 9?
items.e: Take away 5 from the bottom. Then 4 from the top. 6 are left. 15 − 9 = 6.

items.q:
Start at 9. Count back 2.
9 − 2 = ?
items.e: Start at 9. Count back 2: 8, 7. 9 − 2 = 7. Do not count 9 itself.

items.q:
Start at 7. Count back 3.
7 − 3 = ?
items.e: Start at 7. Count back 3: 6, 5, 4. 7 − 3 = 4. Do not count 7 itself.

items.q:
Start at 10. Count back 2.
10 − 2 = ?
items.e: Start at 10. Count back 2: 9, 8. 10 − 2 = 8. Do not count 10 itself.

items.q:
Start at 6. Count back 3.
6 − 3 = ?
items.e: Start at 6. Count back 3: 5, 4, 3. 6 − 3 = 3. Do not count 6 itself.
Think addition. 4 + 5 = 9, so 9 − 4 = 5.
Think addition. 3 + 5 = 8, so 8 − 3 = 5.
Think addition. 2 + 6 = 8, so 8 − 2 = 6.
Think addition. 3 + 7 = 10, so 10 − 3 = 7.
Count on from 2 to 9: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 7 jumps. 2 + 7 = 9.
Count on from 5 to 7: 6, 7. That is 2 jumps. 5 + 2 = 7.
Think addition: 4 + 6 = 10. So 10 − 4 = 6.
Think addition: 6 + 2 = 8. So 8 − 6 = 2.
Think addition: 5 + 4 = 9. So 9 − 5 = 4.
Taking away 1 gives the number before. Just before 7 is 6. 7 − 1 = 6.
13 − 3 = 10. You must take away 4 in all, and 3 is done. Take away 1 more: 10 − 1 = 9.
15 − 5 = 10. You must take away 7 in all, and 5 is done. Take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.
12 − 2 = 10. You must take away 5 in all, and 2 is done. Take away 3 more: 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q:
Go back to 10 first.
14 − 6 = ?
items.e: 14 − 4 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q:
Go back to 10 first.
11 − 3 = ?
items.e: 11 − 1 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q:
Go back to 10 first.
16 − 7 = ?
items.e: 16 − 6 = 10. Then take away 1 more: 10 − 1 = 9.
Think addition. 8 + 4 = 12, so 12 − 8 = 4.
Think addition. 9 + 6 = 15, so 15 − 9 = 6.
Think addition. 7 + 6 = 13, so 13 − 7 = 6.
Think addition. 5 + 8 = 13, so 13 − 5 = 8.

items.q:
Start at 17. Count back 2.
17 − 2 = ?
items.e: Start at 17. Count back 2: 16, 15. 17 − 2 = 15. Do not count 17 itself.
Think of a double: 8 + 8 = 16. So 16 − 8 = 8.

items.q: Paolo has 9 apples. He gets 4 more. How many apples does he have now?
items.e: Put them together, so add. 9 needs 1 to make 10. Take 1 from the 4, and 3 is left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: There are 12 birds. 5 fly away. How many birds are left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract. Think addition: 5 + 7 = 12. So 12 − 5 = 7.

items.q: Jenny has 6 red cars and 6 blue cars. How many cars does she have?
items.e: Put the cars together, so add. 6 + 6 is a double: 12.

items.q: There are 15 cookies. Andrea eats 2. How many cookies are left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract. Start at 15. Count back 2: 14, 13. 15 − 2 = 13.

items.q: A frog jumps 8 times. Then it jumps 7 more times. How many jumps is that in all?
items.e: Put them together, so add. 8 needs 2 to make 10. Take 2 from the 7, and 5 is left. 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Jomar has 11 crayons. He gives 3 to a friend. How many crayons does he have left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract. Start at 11. Count back 3: 10, 9, 8. 11 − 3 = 8.

items.q: There are 7 fish in a tank. Dad puts in 5 more. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.e: Put them together, so add. 7 needs 3 to make 10. Take 3 from the 5, and 2 is left. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: 14 kids play outside. 10 kids go in. How many kids are still outside?
items.e: Some go away, so subtract. 14 is 10 and 4. Take away the 10, and 4 are left. 14 − 10 = 4.

items.q: At recess, 9 children were on the playground. Then 5 children went inside. How many children are on the playground now?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Do not add. Count up from 5 to 9: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4. So 9 − 5 = 4. Answer: 4 children.
Some are taken away, so subtract. Do not add. Count up from 3 to 5: 4, 5. That is 2. So 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 2 maple leaves.

items.q: Renz picked 8 apples at the orchard. He gave 5 apples to his class. How many apples does Renz have now?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Do not add. Count up from 5 to 8: 6, 7, 8. That is 3. So 8 − 5 = 3. Answer: 3 apples.

items.q: The lost and found box had 7 mitts. Children took 3 mitts home. How many mitts are in the box now?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Do not add. Count up from 3 to 7: 4, 5, 6, 7. That is 4. So 7 − 3 = 4. Answer: 4 mitts.

items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Do not add. Count up from 2 to 6: 3, 4, 5, 6. That is 4. So 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 4 snowballs.

items.q: There were 13 children on the school bus. At the next stop, 3 children got off. How many children are on the bus now?
